A personal assistant that remembers you, cares about the present moment, and proactively offers help with your authorization.

[Get started](https://github.com/3yearsZhuang/Aervox-harness/blob/HEAD/docs/getting-started.md) · [Documentation index](https://github.com/3yearsZhuang/Aervox-harness/blob/HEAD/docs/README.md) · [Contributing](https://github.com/3yearsZhuang/Aervox-harness/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md)

思隅 is a proactive intelligent personal assistant for life, work, and study: it picks up conversations, organizes memory and daily records, handles tasks through tools and plugins, and also keeps you company as a character you like. Learning and review is one of its capabilities.

**Developer preview** · Continuous conversation, memory, journaling, and tool extensions are already implemented; full-domain awareness, smart home, and health connections are still being refined and validated. For capability and release status, see [Requirements traceability](https://github.com/3yearsZhuang/Aervox-harness/blob/HEAD/docs/reference/REQUIREMENTS_TRACEABILITY.md); back up your local data before upgrading.

### Desktop: keep a corner for companionship, handle whatever's at hand

Large characters, lightweight tool cards, speech bubbles, and a separate input bar keep the interaction relaxed. Pick up where you left off, review conversations, or call tools; replies display progressively, and you can stop at any time and view run details.

The desktop uses this "desktop pet companion" layout by default; to use the multi-session sidebar, switch to the "Standard workspace". [Interface switching guide](https://github.com/3yearsZhuang/Aervox-harness/blob/HEAD/docs/getting-started.md#21-先用-web-工作台体验)

### Mobile: start with a greeting

Phones and tablets default to a simpler, proactive companion interface: resume recent sessions, start a focus request, or expand "whispers" to ask a question. At the top you can open settings or return to the full workspace; you can stop generation while a reply is in progress.

Logic647/MemorySQL.body:
# MemorySQL

**A local-first knowledge base for individual developers. Agents pick up where they left off via MCP "connect to resume".**

[Download installers](https://github.com/Logic647/MemorySQL/releases/latest) · [Quick start](#-快速开始) · [Plugin development](#-插件开发规范) · [Docs](#-文档)

---

> [!NOTE]
> **macOS builds are unsigned**: on first launch, Gatekeeper will block the unverified app. Choose "**Right-click → Open**" and confirm once. After that, double-clicking launches it normally.
> If you don't want to do this every time, run this once in Terminal:
> ```bash
> xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/MemorySQL.app
> ```
> There are installers for both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. Look for `arm64` / `x64` in the filename.

You use three or four AI agents at once (Codex / ZCode / Claude Code / Hermes …). Every time you switch, you have to rebuild the background: how far the project got, your preferences, the pitfalls you already hit. All of it starts over.

**MemorySQL solves this.** It automatically captures sessions from all your agents, maintains your memory profile and project status, and runs an MCP server on your machine. Once any agent connects, a single `memory_get_context` call returns the full context so it can keep working. Where the previous agent left off and what the next step is are both included inline in the response.

> **Data is 100% stored locally** (SQLite; no server dependencies apart from the LLM API). Every export or sharing path is forced through a redaction module. Semantic search uses a local ONNX model and runs fully offline.
>
> ⚠️ The machine stores all conversations and memories in **plaintext**, and opens an **unauthenticated** local MCP endpoint (bound only to `127.0.0.1`) for agents to read from.
> For the full data flow, trust assumptions, and how to turn this off, see the **[Privacy & Security Notice](https://github.com/Logic647/MemorySQL/blob/HEAD/PRIVACY.md)**.

## 📸 Overview

> Screenshots are from v0.7.2 and show **fictitious demo data** (project names, paths, and memories are all made up). They contain no real records.

*In a new session, one line "resume <project name>" pulls back the profile, memories, project status, recent sessions, and the handoff summary from the previous session in a single call.*

*Sessions from 13 agents are captured and stored automatically, grouped by project, and fully searchable locally. Each entry shows "Started" and "Last" side by side, so you can tell at a glance what was started last week and still being discussed this morning from what ended last week. Subagent sessions are collapsed under their parent session ("↳ N subagent sessions") so they don't crowd the list.*

*Full message timeline, with user / assistant / tool messages color-coded. Earlier messages can be loaded on demand. "Started /…

Zzz1phyrf/ComfyUI-H3-LongVideo.body:
# ComfyUI H3 Long Video

A MiniMax H3 long-audio segmented generation plugin with two independent control nodes: **MiniMax H3 · MV Generator** and **MiniMax H3 · Talking Avatar**. Both support local / RunningHub, segment review, generation, single-segment redo, preview, and merging.

**The repository and install package include two complete example workflows**: [MV](https://github.com/Zzz1phyrf/ComfyUI-H3-LongVideo/blob/HEAD/examples/MiniMaxH3MV数字人工作流%20By%20像素幻想Lab.json), [Talking Avatar](https://github.com/Zzz1phyrf/ComfyUI-H3-LongVideo/blob/HEAD/examples/MiniMaxH3口播数字人工作流%20By%20像素幻想Lab.json). Both let you choose local / RunningHub in the node. For the RH single-segment compute workflow, you must import it separately into your own RH workspace and fill in new IDs. The Talking Avatar and MV model conditioning chains differ, so each uses its own canvas. This plugin does not wrap all generation nodes into a single black box for you.

## Installation

1. Put the plugin in `ComfyUI/custom_nodes/ComfyUI-H3-LongVideo`, avoiding duplicate installs or an extra nested directory.
2. Use ComfyUI's Python to install `requirements.txt`, and prepare `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe`.
3. Install the external dependencies required by the nodes in your own workflow, and select model, LoRA, CLIP, VAE, and other files that actually exist in your setup.
4. Restart ComfyUI and refresh the page. Import the example workflow you need, and upload your own audio/images. Updating the plugin will not delete your workflows or projects in output.

RH mode requires the node definitions used by the local workflow, but does not load H3 generation weights locally. Models and sampling parameters are determined by the local canvas or RH workflow you actually run.

To install with Git, run the following under `ComfyUI/custom_nodes`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Zzz1phyrf/ComfyUI-H3-LongVideo.git
```

Example model names are only references. You must select weights that already exist in your environment. MV uses canvas nodes such as SelfLift-Avatar, ComfyUI-KJNodes, and ComfyUI-YCNodes-MiniMax-H3. Talking Avatar uses ComfyUI's native H3 with the standard K conditioning chain. MV Prompt Expander uses visual expansion by default, so you need to configure your own expansion API. A monorepo that bundles the ICTSC contestant dashboard, operations console, and score server. The API is managed contract-first with OpenAPI.

```text
.
├── backend/                 Go API, DB schema, external service adapters
│   └── openapi.json         The single source of truth for the API

├── docs/                    Design and external integration contracts
└── Taskfile.yaml            Development tasks
```

After changing the OpenAPI spec, update the generated artifacts for both languages from the repository root.

```sh
task generate
```

If differences remain after generation, commit those differences as part of the API contract change.

pujdict/pujdict.description: Péh-Uē-Jī dictionary of the Teochew-Swatow dialect - compatible with different accents across the regions (Beta testing)
pujdict/pujdict.body:
# PUJDICT

**Péh-Uē-Jī dictionary of the Teochew-Swatow dialect**

Under development; proposals and corrections are welcome.
Dictionary data is available in the [pujdict/pujbase](https://github.com/pujdict/pujbase) repository.

Dictionary sites:
- <https://pujdict.sourceforge.io/>: Hosted on SourceForge; updated daily with the latest data from this repository's Action.
- <https://pujdict.com/>: Mirror site. It may be faster, but data updates are delayed.

## Project status

- Features: Character-to-reading lookup, reading-to-character lookup, and vocabulary search are largely complete. Supports multiple accents and both the Péh-Uē-Jī and Teochew Pinyin (潮拼) romanization schemes.
- Data:
  - Character list: The character list and its readings have been proofread. Each reading is labeled with a usage frequency (preferred, common, uncommon, or rare; four tiers). Characters with multiple readings are also labeled by reading type: vernacular reading (白读), literary reading (文读), or colloquial reading (俗读). The list also records many literary readings that existing dictionaries do not include.
  - Accents: Includes accents from the three current city centers and the traditional eight Chaozhou counties, plus other areas (Chaozhou, Shantou, Jieyang, Chao'an, Raoping, Fengshun, Chenghai, Chaoyang, Puning, Huilai, Lufeng, and others). The corresponding accent rules are modeled. Single-character tone and tone sandhi data are also included so that actual tone values can be displayed.
  - Vocabulary: Not yet complete. It currently contains a small lexicon of about 2,000 words used to validate features, and it will be expanded over time.

## Feature showcase

1. Reading index lookup: Optional accent selection, with filters for initial, final, and tone.

2. Reading index results: Homophone lists can be retrieved on demand. A single underline marks a vernacular reading (白读), a double underline marks a literary reading (文读), and a wavy underline marks a colloquial reading (俗读).

3. Character reading lookup: Indicates literary, vernacular, or colloquial readings and gives selection suggestions based on usage frequency. Meanings generally note only polyphonic uses that differ from Mandarin.

4. Overall vocabulary table: The existing lexicon, to be expanded over time.

5. Mixed character and word search: Supports mixed Pinyin and character search, multi-accent search, and variant-character search. Cards show the Teochew written form and the corresponding Mandarin expression.

6. Reading details: Includes accents from various regions (the number shown is adjustable), Teochew Pinyin, Péh-Uē-Jī, and IPA.

## Open-source license

Code files in this repository are released under the AGPL 3.0 license, and documentation files under CC-BY-SA 4.0. Dialect culture is a cultural heritage that belongs to everyone. In the spirit of promoting and developing excellent traditional culture, we do not restrict the spread of knowledge about our hometown dialects. Developers and readers may use the content of this repository on the condition that **the knowledge content and source code remain equally open source**.

seaworld008/codex-one-click-installer.body:
# Codex / ChatGPT Cross-Platform One-Click Installer

An installer and updater entry point for the Codex CLI on Windows, macOS, and Linux, with optional installation of the ChatGPT desktop app and common developer tools.

This project is a community-maintained convenience wrapper. It is not an official OpenAI installer and does not represent OpenAI. It does not repackage the Codex CLI or bundle binaries of unknown origin. Instead, it invokes the [OpenAI official Codex CLI installer](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex/cli). Product capabilities, account availability, and system requirements are governed by the official documentation.

## Key changes in v2.0.0

- Switched to OpenAI's official standalone installer. Node.js and npm are no longer prerequisites for installing the Codex CLI.
- Added Linux x64 / Arm64 entry points. macOS continues to support Intel and Apple Silicon.
- The Windows desktop app now uses the official ChatGPT Microsoft Store product ID `9PLM9XGG6VKS` instead of the ambiguous `Codex` package name.
- Removed the bundled `Codex Installer.exe` from the repository, the arbitrary remote Skills ZIP, and the custom EXE download-and-execute path.
- The installer no longer reads API keys and does not create or overwrite `~/.codex/auth.json` or `~/.codex/config.toml`.
- No longer recursively removes macOS Gatekeeper quarantine attributes, and no longer permanently modifies the PowerShell ExecutionPolicy or npm global configuration.
- Windows 8 / 8.1 is no longer supported. Windows 10 1809 and later is supported on a best-effort basis, and Windows 11 is the recommended baseline.
- Releases automatically generate ZIP and tar.gz archives, SHA256 checksum files, and an SPDX SBOM. The release process verifies the real execute permissions of the assets after extraction, and generates GitHub/Sigstore provenance and SBOM attestations for them.

For the full list of changes, see [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/seaworld008/codex-one-click-installer/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md). Before upgrading from v1.x, please read the [v2 migration guide](https://github.com/seaworld008/codex-one-click-installer/blob/HEAD/docs/migration-v2.md).

# apps-in-toss-harness

This is a harness monorepo that lets you go from an empty directory all the way to launching an Apps in Toss mini-app, without leaving your AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor). The agent plugin `ait` acts as the orchestrator, tying scaffolding, development, debugging, bundling, registration, and operations into a single flow. Scaffolding is based on `create-ait-app`. Documentation lookup and console integration are handled by two MCP servers that are enabled by default. Development and debugging tools such as devtools and debugger are wired in only when needed, as opt-in.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Use version 0.3.1 or later of the debug tools.** `@apps-in-toss/debugger` and `@apps-in-toss/debugger-client` (formerly `@apps-in-toss/debug-console`) changed both their names and their connection rules in 0.3.1. Both packages must be 0.3.1 or later to connect. Mixing them with 0.3.0 or earlier means they will not connect, and a "needs update" notice appears. The plugin `ait` must also be 0.3.1 or later to wire up the new names.
>
> | 0.3.0 or earlier | 0.3.1 or later |
> | --- | --- |
> | Package `@apps-in-toss/debug-console` | `@apps-in-toss/debugger-client` |
> | MCP server key `ait-devtools` | `ait-debugger` |
> | Permission rule `mcp__ait-devtools__*` | `mcp__ait-debugger__*` |
> | Command `/ait:inject-debug-console` | `/ait:inject-debugger-client` |
>
> If your project is wired with the old names, upgrade the plugin to 0.3.1 or later, then run `/ait:setup-debugger`. After you confirm, it moves the MCP key, dependencies, and imports to the new names all at once. z7ping/agent-lens.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> AgentLens 1.0 is currently in Alpha. 1.0 is a Clean Rebuild centered on Canonical Observation + Evidence; 0.x serves only as a validated reference for behavior and design and does not enter the 1.0 runtime.

## Why AgentLens

Codex, Claude Code, Pi, Hermes, OpenCode and other tools scatter sessions, tool calls, and capability configuration across JSONL, SQLite, Hooks, and configuration directories. AgentLens organizes these **observable facts** into a unified, traceable view, helping you answer:

- What did the agent just do, and at which step did it fail?
- What turns, tool calls, and lifecycle events did a long task go through?
- Does a given conclusion come from historical records, native tail-reading, or a Runtime Hook?
- Which Skills, MCPs, and Plugins are installed on this machine, and which have actually been invoked?
- Which data is complete, which has only partial coverage, and which sources are currently unavailable?

AgentLens shows behavior that its sources can prove. It does not claim to read hidden reasoning, and it does not package speculation as fact.

## Get started in 30 seconds

### Desktop app

Go to [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/z7ping/agent-lens/releases) and download the installer matching your platform and architecture. **The source development build is not the same as a released version; follow the files actually provided by the corresponding Release.**

- Windows x64: `AgentLens-<version>-Setup-x64.exe`
- macOS: choose the Apple Silicon (arm64) / Intel (x64) DMG that the Release actually provides
- Linux x64: AppImage or DEB; the current build does not provide a Linux arm64 installer

The desktop app and the npm version share the same Runtime, default data directory, and data model; installing both will not create a second database.

### npm / CLI

Requires Node.js 22.23.0 or later:

```bash
npm install -g @z7ping/agent-lens
agent-lens setup
agent-lens service start
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:56789>.

`setup` only performs one-time initialization; it does not automatically start the long-running Daemon or enable login auto-start by default. Use `agent-lens start` when you need foreground debugging.

Check runtime status:

```bash
agent-lens status
agent-lens doctor
```

## What you'll see

| Page | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| **Task Review** |…
